title: Routing Channel-Patch Dependencies in Time Series Forecasting with Graph Spectral Decomposition
abstract: Time series forecasting has attracted significant attention in the field of AI. Previous works have revealed that the Channel-Independent (CI) strategy improves forecasting performance by modeling each channel individually, but it often suffers from poor generalization and overlooks meaningful inter-channel interactions. Conversely, Channel-Dependent (CD) strategies aggregate all channels, which may introduce irrelevant information and lead to oversmoothing. Despite recent progress, few existing methods offer the flexibility to adaptively balance CI and CD strategies in response to varying channel dependencies. To address this, we propose a generic plugin xCPD, that can adaptively model the channel-patch dependencies from the perspective of graph spectral decomposition. Specifically, xCPD first projects multivariate signals into the frequency domain using a shared graph Fourier basis, and groups patches into low-, mid-, and high-frequency bands based on their spectral energy responses. xCPD then applies a channel-adaptive routing mechanism that dynamically adjusts the degree of inter-channel interaction for each patch, enabling selective activation of frequency-specific experts. This facilitates fine-grained, input-aware modeling of smooth trends, local fluctuations, and abrupt transitions. xCPD can be seamlessly integrated on top of existing CI and CD forecasting models, consistently enhancing both accuracy and generalization across benchmarks.
problem: Time series forecasting struggles to adaptively balance channel-independent and channel-dependent strategies because different channels exhibit varying levels of meaningful inter-channel interactions.
approach: xCPD is a generic plugin that projects multivariate signals into the frequency domain using graph Fourier basis, groups patches by spectral energy into frequency bands, and applies channel-adaptive routing with frequency-specific experts.
contribution: Consistently enhances both accuracy and generalization across benchmarks when integrated into existing channel-independent and channel-dependent models.
